steps.text: Rhodes Island Ursus Outpost

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: *Yawn*... Morning meeting after hitting the hay at four last night? Gimme a break...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Why don't you look tired at all, Sussurro?

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: We were taught at school to put on a proper appearance at work, so—

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: So you had three cups of espresso first thing in the morning. Not exactly a healthy lifestyle, Operator Sussurro.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Ahem. Now that Hibiscus is here, let's start the meeting.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Wait, before that we need to introduce our newest colleague. Come on in, Operator Myrrh.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: G-Good morning. I'm Myrrh, and I've just been made an operator. You can also call me by my real name, Adelaide.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: She's been assigned to us after completing her internship. Operator Myrrh, meet Operator Gavial.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Good morning, Miss Gavial.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Just call me Gavial.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Glad to have you onboard. We can always use more medics. Can't even remember the last time I got a good night's sleep.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: We're doing what we can to recruit more. Just try not to scare away the rookies before they even get settled in.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I-I'm ready for it. Dr. Kal'tsit told me that the job of a medic is really tough.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Good to hear you've gotten advance warning. Things are really hectic around here.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: That's Operator Sussurro next to Gavial. She'll be your supervisor.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: G-Good morning, Miss Sussurro. I look forward to working with you.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Right. Just so you know, us operators don't really call each other 'Miss'. And don't worry, we'll ease you in gradually.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I-I'll do my best. Please let me know whenever I'm doing something wrong.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Seriously, we're just thankful to have you here to take on some of the workload.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Ahem. Then shall we get to today's schedule?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: The refugees' conditions are all under control on my end. If all goes well, we should be able to release some of them by next month.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: What about you, Hibiscus?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Most of the patients are fine, except for one.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Who's that?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mrs. Luba.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Is she doing badly?

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Her condition isn't all that bad, but she's been refusing treatment.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Wait. She's sick, but doesn't want to get treated?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: She's a superstitious one. When she first came, she told me not to waste my time because her village shaman told her she wouldn't live past seventy.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Seems a little dodgy...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: She believes every word of it, though, even seeing everyday events as signs that the end is near.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: She practically fled when she saw Kuro outside last Friday.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Apparently, seeing a black Originium slug is an omen that death approaches.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: So that's why she was crying all day. Wouldn't even take her meals.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: (Whisper) Maybe...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: It's just a tough situation all around.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Excuse me, Sussurro? May I try talking to her?

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Are you sure? It takes more than medical expertise to work with a patient like her. You need communication skills too.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: There are many superstitious people where I'm from, and I've picked up a few tricks to deal with them.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Are you sure about this?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Why not let her have a go? Not like we've got any better ideas.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: P-Please. I want to do this.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Very well then, give it a shot. Gavial, could you bring up Mrs. Luba's patient history for her?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Thank you, Gavial.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Are we sure about this, Sussurro? I still think we should think it through.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Gavial's right though, we don't have any other ideas.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Be sure to report back if you encounter any trouble with her. We'll do what we can to support you.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Thank you. I'll do my best.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Welp, then follow me, Myrrh.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Was there anything else you wanted to say, Hibiscus?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Er, well, I'm still a little worried. Dr. Kal'tsit told me about some of her... quirks.

steps.name: Sussurro
steps.text: Such as?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Let's just say that she has some superstitions of her own.
Rhodes Island Field Hospital

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Mrs. Luba should be here...
Enough! Take it away! I don't need it.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Excuse me, what's going on in there? She sounded angry.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Ah, you must be the new doctor.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I spilled a jar of salt. Apparently that's a taboo in Ursus, like it's really unlucky for them, so she's fuming mad.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Maybe you should come back later, let her get it out of her system.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Don't worry, I'm just here to say hi.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I said I don't need it! What are y— Oh.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Good morning, Mrs. Luba.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: And who are you?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: My name is Myrrh, and I'm your new doctor. I'll be working with you to treat your symptoms—

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Get out, girl, and take your medicine with you! Stop wasting your time on me and let me go in peace!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Well, Mrs. Luba, I, er, didn't bring any medicine today.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Then what are you here for? Trying to talk me out of my 'superstitions' again?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: No, not at all. I've never been very good at talking.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Then, what? You here to gawk?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Well, I, er, brought something for you. It's a lucky charm from home that I've been carrying for years. My clan chief told me that it brings good luck to whoever wears it.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: (Takes the charm from her neck and gives it to the old woman)

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Sorry if it's a little worn.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: A little thing like this... Well, thank you anyway.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: It's gotten me out of trouble so many times over the years.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I didn't think you young folk believed in these things anymore. Everyone's always on about 'science' and 'evidence' and that only backwards, uneducated folk like me still believe this stuff.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: People always tell me that I'm superstitious too. I always go into a room with my left foot first, and the first thing I do when I move to a new place is set up some fowlbeast feathers.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I'm a little afraid to even talk about these things with my peers. Many of them graduated from med school, and they just sneer at this stuff.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: They're too young to believe in fate. When you get to my age, you realize that some things that are just out of the hands of us mortals.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: When I was little, a fortune teller said I was fated for hardship for the rest of my life.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I didn't believe it back then, but look at me now.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: My village got caught up in a Catastrophe, my only daughter's dead from it, and now I'm sick in my old age. I'm not long for this world.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Oh, Mika... How could you leave your mother all alone like this?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: (Takes the old woman's hands) Mrs. Luba...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: What is it? Bored with my griping?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: No, not at all. I want to know more. Tell me about your daughter. Considering how well you've aged, your daughter must have been truly beautiful.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: And here you said you weren't any good at talking.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Right, my Mika was the jewel of the village. Her golden hair was like silk, so smooth and shiny.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Oh, my poor girl... life means nothing without her.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Everything tastes so bland these days. And each day is just about making it to the next one.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Would you like some sour apple pie?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Where's this coming from? What is it anyway?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: It's a new item on the canteen menu. The tangy flavor really works up the appetite.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I'm not hungry. Just stay and chat with me for a bit.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Go on then, I'm listening.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Mika always loved apples. Not the sweet ones, but the sour ones.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I could never handle anything too sour. It makes my teeth curl.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: My Mika always had such great teeth...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: The air outside smells so fresh after last night's snow, doesn't it?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Stopping by so early? Don't you have work to do?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Don't worry, my schedule isn't that packed.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: You doctors always seem so busy. Didn't think you'd have time to listen to me babble.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Hehe, would you rather I didn't come then?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Girl...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: To be honest, it's good to see you.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I feel the same way. I couldn't stop thinking about you.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Why? What do you see in a washed-up old woman like me?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: You're about my grandma's age, and you even look a little alike. Seeing you reminds me of her.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: If I had a granddaughter, she'd be about your age now.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: You must've really loved your grandma then.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Yes. She taught me everything I know about wild forest herbs, and how to use them for medicine.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: She also taught me how to find my way, so I'm never lost no matter where I go.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Do you miss home?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Very much.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Me too... but I won't see it again. And I won't ever see my Mika either.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Don't cry, Mrs. Luba. She'll come back to you, someday.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: What are you on about? How can somebody who's dead come back to me?!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Please, don't get angry. It's just what we say in my clan.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: We believe that the spirit of the woods guides the dead to the Great Green, where they become one with nature.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Whenever someone in my clan dies, we gather by the river and send down a little boat holding a candle, in order to light the way back for them.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Even if what you said is true, and Mika really came back... what would she become?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I don't know. Maybe the stars and the wind in the sky, or the snow and the rain on a lake.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Or the grass under our feet, soft and lovely...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: But the land's so big. How could I find her?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: We... we can't find them ourselves. We can only wait for them to find us.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: That's why our chief leads the guiding dance at funerals, so that those who are gone can find their way back and reunite with us.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Girl...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Do you... know the dance? Can you dance for her? For Mika?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I want to see her. No matter what she's become.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Alright.
Myrrh did not know how bad her dancing was.
Her steps were slow and out of sync with her arms. Even a farmer tilling the fields would look more elegant and coordinated.
Her movements were clumsy and comical, like a baby fowlbeast flailing in the snow.
But Luba did not laugh. As Myrrh made circles in the snow, waving her arms, a cold morning wind brushed against the hair on Luba's brow.
She closed her eyes and felt the air rush past her cheek. Something warm filled her eyes.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Girl...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: (Falls) T-The world's spinning... I'm spinning...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Mrs. Luba? W-What is it?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Let's go back. I'm in the mood for some sour apple pie.
One month later...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: There you are, Adelaide. Good to see you one last time before I leave.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Your symptoms are under control, and should remain stable for the foreseeable future. As long as you watch your diet and take the suppressant regularly.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Thank you so much for doing all this for an old sack of bones like me.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I'm just doing my job. Oh, before I forget... here, I got you a sour apple pie to eat on the way.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Aw, aren't you just a sweetheart? You remember my favorite.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I'll see you off then.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Sure thing, love.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Before I came here, I was all outta hope. I would just sit on my bed all day, wishing to kick the bucket already.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Until I met you.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Now I can feel Mika by my side all the time. I see her whenever I look at the mountains, the trees, the flowers, the grass, the rain, the snow...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I want to see more, to keep seeing her.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: And to do that, I've gotta keep on living.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I'm sure she'd be happy. Take care, Mrs. Luba. I'm not sure how often we can see each other again...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Come now, pull yourself together.
Myrrh smiles and takes the old woman's hand. The two of them walk quietly over the snow.
Only when they have arrived at the village gate does the old woman hesitantly begin to speak.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Adelaide... let me ask you something. Answer me honestly.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: All that stuff you told me... is it really true?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Mrs. Luba...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I mean, do you believe it? Be honest.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: When I was little, the chief would brew me medicine whenever I was sick. And I always got better soon after taking it.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I used to think it was so amazing.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: But when I came to the landship, I began to study its composition, to learn medicine in a systematic matter.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: That's when I found that it was just a common herbal drink, with no special effects.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: So I put away my research on it, and turned to studying other medicines.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: But I still find myself making it whenever I get sick, simply out of habit.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: And not just when I'm sick - I do it when an experiment didn't go well, or when I can't sleep, or when I scrape my knee after a fall.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Why do you keep drinking it, even though you know it has no effect?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I'm not sure why... sorry.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Why... why, indeed?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Is it all true, Harmonia? Does this dance really bring the dead back to our side? Does the Great Green really exist?

steps.name: Harmonia
steps.text: Adelaide... I can't answer that question, because I don't know either.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Why do you join the chief in the guiding dance then, if you don't know sure?

steps.name: Harmonia
steps.text: Because I hope that it's true, and that someday we'll reunite with the ones who have left us.

steps.name: Harmonia
steps.text: That's why I dance.

steps.name: Harmonia
steps.text: This land has too many troubles and hardships. The helpless must learn to help themselves, and the lost must learn to find their own answers.

steps.name: Harmonia
steps.text: That's why we place our hopes on the ethereal, on the supernatural.

steps.name: Harmonia
steps.text: That's why we have superstitions.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: But, Harmonia...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I suppose it becomes true if you believe in it.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Never mind. Who cares if it's true or not, at my age?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: There isn't much I can give you, but take this necklace that my man left me.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: No, I can't accept that.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Just take it. It's nothing valuable.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I appreciate it, but the Medical Department has rules against accepting gifts from patients.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: It'll bring you good luck. Take it, girl, and take care.
As she watches Mrs. Luba leave, Adelaide rubs her eyes and recalls sitting by Harmonia, gazing at the river in the distance.

a.text: That night, the canopy was bathed in the silver light of the twin moons, shining through the gaps in the leaves.
The night wind carried the wailing of the clanspeople as they pushed floating candles into the river one after another.
Their light brightened the night sky, forming a band of radiance embracing the people gathered on the bank.
